facts.raw_span: fever and severe arthralgia one month earlier
Primary HIV infection, tuberculosis, sarcoidosis, and syphilis had been ruled out
Stromal immune ring formation with underlying keratic precipitates
Aqueous tap PCR results: Positive for Chikungunya virus with weak viral load
Negative for human herpesviruses 1 and 2, varicella-zoster virus, cytomegalovirus, adenovirus, and rubella virus

concepts.why: The patient's ocular symptoms, including bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation, along with the positive Chikungunya virus PCR results and IgM serologic test, support this diagnosis.

The patient's ocular symptoms, including bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation, along with the positive IgM serologic test, suggest post-infectious ocular complications.

Although the patient's PCR results were negative for human herpesviruses, the clinical presentation, including bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation, could be consistent with HSV ocular infection.

The patient's ocular symptoms, including bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation, along with the negative PCR results for other viruses, could suggest VZV ocular infection.

The patient's ocular symptoms, including bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation, could be consistent with Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis, an autoimmune ocular disorder.
Although sarcoidosis was ruled out, the patient's periorbital hyperpigmentation and ocular symptoms could be consistent with sarcoidosis-related ocular disease.
Although tuberculosis was ruled out, the patient's periorbital hyperpigmentation and ocular symptoms could be consistent with tuberculosis-related ocular disease.
Although syphilis was ruled out, the patient's periorbital hyperpigmentation and ocular symptoms could be consistent with syphilis-related ocular disease.
It explains the uncovered finding of bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and negative laboratory results for other viruses.

rationales.F03: Fever and arthralgia are common symptoms of Chikungunya virus infection.
rationales.F04: Neurological complications can occur in Chikungunya virus infection.
rationales.F05: Periorbital hyperpigmentation is a possible symptom of Chikungunya virus infection.
rationales.F08: Bilateral punctate superficial keratitis is a possible symptom of Chikungunya virus ocular infection.
rationales.F09: Stromal immune ring formation with underlying keratic precipitates is a possible symptom of Chikungunya virus ocular infection.
rationales.F10: Positive PCR result for Chikungunya virus is a strong indicator of Chikungunya virus infection.
rationales.F11: Positive IgM CHIKV serologic test is a strong indicator of Chikungunya virus infection.
rationales.F12: Negative PCR results for other viruses rule out other possible causes of ocular infection.
